title_as_printed: Isopiestic molalities m of {(1 - y)NaCl + yLiCl}(aq)
footnotes_as_printed: not captured (no footnotes on the table; text: last digit of most molalities is not significant but given for consistency and to avoid round-off error; molalities accurate to better than 0.2 per cent)
pressure_note: not stated (isopiestic equilibrium with a common vapour phase at constant temperature and pressure; pressure not reported)

value.what: isopiestic molality of the pure NaCl(aq) reference solution in equilibrium with the four mixed solutions of the same printed row; the paper uses it as the isopiestic standard

mixture_columns.what: isopiestic molality of {(1-y)NaCl + yLiCl}(aq) at that y, equilibrated with the NaCl reference of the same row
isopiestic molality of {(1-y)NaCl + yLiCl}(aq) at that y, equilibrated with the NaCl reference of the same row
isopiestic molality of {(1-y)NaCl + yLiCl}(aq) at that y, equilibrated with the NaCl reference of the same row
isopiestic molality of {(1-y)NaCl + yLiCl}(aq) at that y, equilibrated with the NaCl reference of the same row

composition.other_species: mixture {(1-y)NaCl + yLiCl}: y is the mole fraction of LiCl in the dissolved salt, printed in the column header; the molality m is that of the mixed solution as printed (total salt molality per kg water, as the table caption m of {(1-y)NaCl+yLiCl}(aq)). LiCl is outside the six-ion set; NaCl is in scope. The y=0 column is pure NaCl(aq), the isopiestic reference. Each mixture column's composition is the header y (y_LiCl in mixture_columns).

conversion_needs: osmotic coefficient of the mixture = phi_NaCl(m_ref) * m_ref / m_mix (Pitzer-Peiper-Busey NaCl reference; not given in the table, not converted here)
molality of a mixture of 1-1 salts: ion molality = total salt molality, so nu is 2 for both NaCl and LiCl
notes: Printed as two side-by-side blocks of five columns (y=0 NaCl reference, then y=0.3023, 0.4565, 0.5751, 0.7142) per row. Stacked here: within each temperature, all left-block rows in printed order, then all right-block rows. Each written row is one isopiestic equilibrium: the five molalities of a row were in equilibrium with each other. Rows per temperature, left/right: 383.19 K 10/9, 413.22 K 8/8, 443.19 K 9/9, 473.18 K 10/10, 498.16 K 10/10, 523.17 K 9/8. The column header 'y=0' above the first left column and '0' above the first right column both denote pure NaCl. Small non-monotonic orderings across y in a few dilute rows (e.g. 473.18 K 2.0726 2.0586 2.0368 2.0379 2.0006) are as printed. Temperatures given as printed to two decimals (K).
